events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...Wisconsin...

Fox River Lower Near New Munster affecting Lake and Kenosha
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Fox River Lower near New Munster.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Floodwaters begin to affect 77th St. in the
Town of Wheatland. Floodwaters are near some homes along Riverside
Dr, Shorewood Dr, and Highway W in the Village of Salem Lakes and
Town of Wheatland areas. Fox River Park boat launch starts to
flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 10.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 11.1 feet this evening. It will then fall
below flood stage tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.0
feet on 03/11/2020.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Iowa...

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Clinton and Scott
Counties.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Water affects many residences along the
river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 12.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to crest at 12.9 feet today. It
will fall to 11.8 feet by Monday evening then rise again to 12.7
feet by Thursday, October 8th.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 25 to 35 kt with frequent gusts up to 45
kt and seas 14 to 18 feet.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) moves north-
northeast and away from the islands, a strong monsoon surge will
continue across the area. Strong to near-gale force winds with
frequent gale-force gusts will continue over Tinian and Saipan
coastal waters, with sustained gale-force winds likely to be
felt over northern coastal waters for the rest of tonight. This
Gale Warning is being issued to replace the Tropical Storm
Warning, which is no longer in effect.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous seas 12 to 16 feet and southwest
winds 20 to 30 kt with occasional gusts up to 40 kt.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM ChST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Hazardous sea conditions are expected to
continue over the coastal waters through early Sunday morning as
a strong monsoon surge continues well south of Typhoon Choi-wan
(26W). This Warning will later be replaced by a Small Craft
Advisory as combined seas gradually diminish below 15 feet.

events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions
with high temperatures in the mid 90s to 102 and warm nights with
low temperatures in the 70s expected. For the Wind Advisory, east
winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 35 mph expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Inland Areas.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT Thursday. For
the Wind Advisory, until 6 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Heat
related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat
events.

Missouri River at Waverly affecting Carroll, Lafayette and Saline
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Missouri River at Waverly.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 23.5 feet, Rural areas along the river which are not
protected by levees flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 24.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 25.7 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late Tuesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Hamblen, TN; Jefferson, TN; Knox, TN; Sevier, TN
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Hamblen County in east Tennessee...
Jefferson County in east Tennessee...
East Central Knox County in east Tennessee...
Northwestern Sevier County in east Tennessee...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 648 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Up
to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sevierville, Jefferson City, Dandridge, White Pine, New Market,
Baneberry, Strawberry Plains and Piedmont.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
